recipes.name: Broiled Scallops
ingredients_raw: 2 tablespoons melted butter, or as needed

steps.text: Preheat the broiler to high heat.
Rinse scallops and place in a shallow baking pan. Sprinkle with 2 tablespoons melted butter, lemon juice, and garlic salt.
Broil in the preheated broiler until scallops begin to turn golden, 6 to 8 minutes. Remove from the oven and serve with extra melted butter on the side for dipping.

raw_recipe.headline: Broiled Scallops
raw_recipe.description: These broiled scallops are flavored with butter, lemon, and garlic salt, then quickly broiled until golden brown and sweet for a quick, easy dinner.

review.reviewBody: The first time I made this I followed the recipe exactly, and it was excellent. The second time, however, it was OUT OF THIS WORLD making the following changes: Instead of broiling, melt the butter in a saucepan over med/high heat. Add the remaining ingredients (except the lemon) and sautee the scallops for approx two minutes on each side. Pour the scallops and the sauce over pilafed rice, squeeze fresh lemon juice over the top, and garnish with a little parsley and a tiny bit of paprika for color. My fiance says this is the best seafood recipe I have ever made!

Absolutely excellent! Only limited by the quality of scallops used. We used cheap-o Sam's frozen scallops because that is what we had on hand..similar to another reviewer, and they still turned out good. (I halved the garlic salt and added garlic powder as another reviewer recommended). My husband often eats scallops when we eat out, and can vouch for the great taste of this unassuming recipe. I rate it 5 for ease and he rates it 5 for taste. A winner!

Delicious! Living in Maryland, I took notice that another reviewer substituted Old Bay Seasoning for the Garlic Salt. I microwaved 4T butter, 4 sliced garlic cloves and 1oz lime juice, then let it stand while I rinsed and patted dry 1.5lb of Sea Scallops. I brushed a large fry pan and the scallops with the butter mixture, put the scallops in the pan and dusted them with Old Bay. I saluted them 4-5 minutes on a side at medium to medium-high until golden brown. They were great!
This was so easy! But, I melted the butter with 2 cloves of fresh minced garlic before pouring into the scallops. Some fresh ground black pepper, a very small amount of salt and there you go!

This must be the simplest dish with the biggest payoff. Gourmet “fast food.” I only had a pound of scallops, so I added a half pound of shrimp and I would do it again for more interest. Perhaps even add a few clams for accent. And why only 2 tablespoons of butter? Add more! Why not use some real pressed garlic instead of garlic salt. It takes no time, and it’s so much better. So I melted the salted butter, garlic, lemon juice, and some red pepper flakes in a little pot, poured over seafood and mixed it throughout; I arranged seafood in individual gratin dishes, put the lightest sprinkle of fine Italian breadcrumbs over it. Comes out bubbling hot, goes from oven right to the table. I added fresh parsley at the end and a little cup of melted butter on each plate. A great company dish but simple enough for any day of the week. A keeper.

So easy! I impulse bought 1/3 lb. of scallops and wanted something easy and fresh -- set them in a ceramic pie pan, sprinkled a little garlic powder (lost the garlic salt!) + a little salt + fresh cracked pepper, squeezed half a lemon over everything (and the excess in the bottom of the pan), and sprayed a good amount of butter over everything (I was out of butter! except for the spray kind my hubby loves). Broiled for 8.5 minutes -- tasty, delicate, perfection.
Simple, simple, simple. My husband the newbie in the kitchen followed this - using real garlic with salt and pepper instead of garlic salt - and made a great dish. Better than a restaurant!

Used 1 Tbsp. garlic powder instead of garlic salt, added 1/2 tsp sea salt, used unsalted butter and Sprinkled with paprika and Parmesan cheese before broiling. 

Didn't need extra butter for dipping.

Recipe is good, as written - but I would never use either powdered garlic or garlic salt! The late James Beard deplored them. Rather than broiling - which can be unreliable, I sautéed fresh minced garlic in my cast iron skillet - heated very hot! - using a combination of butter & olive oil. Remove the garlic before it turns brown, then add the scallops. Cook very quickly, remove to a serving dish, sprinkle with salt, the lemon juice and the pan drippings.

Easy and delicious!! I have to watch my sodium intake so I chopped a clove of garlic and put it into a pan with the butter on low heat. While it was melting, it infused the butter with the garlic. I added a pinch of sea salt at the end. I served it over fresh spinach and the sauce created by the butter, garlic, lemon and scallops, I poured over the spinach so it wilted just a bit. AMAZING!!

Very, very good! Melted butter in a sauce pan and added the garlic. Tossed scallops in it and then added them to all the dry ingredients which were in a large baggie. Tossed them until coated and placed in baking pan. Drizzled remaining butter over the top with a little lemon juice. Served over Pasta Roni garlic and butter noodles. Cooked at 400 for 20 minutes. Perfectly done. Would make again. Hubby really enjoyed.
I needed to broil them longer. I just hate to overcook scallops! I will make this recipe again.
Felt the scallops were a little soggy. I did dry them off after rinsing. I think I will try them again with some different spices.
So easy. Delicious.
Quick, convenient, not bad, but not great.
I Love Scallops, but was having a hard time getting them just like I wanted them. This makes them perfect and delicious. Note, I use granulated garlic instead of garlic salt.
So what did I do wrong? Of course the butter burned, and thank god the smoke alarm didn’t go off. Sorry this recipe makes no sense especially when you can pan fry so easily?

Delicious, but instead of sprinkling on butter and lemon i placed the dried scallops in a bowl and added the butter, lemon juice and garlic salt in a bowl and then put them into the pan. I used a spatula to get every bit of butter and lemon seasoning into the pan with the scallops. So good!
My husbands dad said that "When it comes to scallops I'm world class"
Turned out absolutely delicious.
